To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the critical stress for twinning in a single crystal of cadmium is raised when the surface of the crystal is covered by a film of cadmium, and is lowered when the surface is covered by a thin film of copper; and (2) the critical stress is not affected by a surface film of cadmium oxide, cadmium sulphide or copper oxide, and is lowered by a thin surface film of copper sulphide.

(i) The stress necessary to cause the first twin to appear in a single crystal of cadmium is greater when a thin surface film (of copper) is present than when the surface is clean; (ii) The number of twins formed in the same crystal increases as the film becomes thicker; (iii) The stress necessary for the formation of the first twin is greater when the surface is covered with a thick film of copper than when it is clean.
